## Load data

```{python}
from IPython.display import display
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv(
    "/home/frederik/github_projects/SNPster/data pipeline/reporting_module/data/multiple_pgs_scores_example.zip",
    compression="zip", sep="\t"
)

#get metadata

meta_data = pd.read_excel(
    "/home/frederik/github_projects/SNPster/data pipeline/reporting_module/data/pgs_all_metadata.xlsx", sheet_name="Scores"
)

publications_meta_data = pd.read_excel(
    "/home/frederik/github_projects/SNPster/data pipeline/reporting_module/data/pgs_all_metadata.xlsx", sheet_name="Publications"
)   




display(df.head())
display(meta_data.head())
display(publications_meta_data.head())

```


## Prepare data


```{python}

#only keep sampleset column != reference

df = df[df["sampleset"] != "reference"]
#remove _hmPOS_GRCh38 in the PGS column value strings

df["PGS"] = df["PGS"].str.replace("_hmPOS_GRCh38", "", regex=False)

print(df.columns)
print(meta_data.columns)
#join metadata on df by the PGS and Polygenic Score (PGS) ID column

df = df.merge(
    meta_data[["Polygenic Score (PGS) ID", "PGS Name", "Reported Trait", "PGS Publication (PGP) ID"]],
    left_on="PGS",
    right_on="Polygenic Score (PGS) ID",
    how="left"
)

print(df.columns)
print(publications_meta_data.columns)

#only keep the values in the "PGS Publication/Study (PGP) ID", whihc are present in the "Polygenic Score (PGS) ID" column of the df
print(df["PGS Publication (PGP) ID"])
print(publications_meta_data["PGS Publication/Study (PGP) ID"])

publications_meta_data = publications_meta_data[
    publications_meta_data["PGS Publication/Study (PGP) ID"].isin(df["PGS Publication (PGP) ID"])
]

publications_meta_data.head()




#make plotly barplot where y = percentile_MostSimilarPop, x = PGS, color = Reported Trait ordered ascending by percentile_MostSimilarPop and transparent background





```


## Plot



```{python}

import plotly.express as px
fig = px.bar(
    df,
    x="PGS",
    y="percentile_MostSimilarPop",
    color="Reported Trait",
    title="Percentile of Most Similar Population for Each PGS",
    category_orders={"PGS": df.sort_values("percentile_MostSimilarPop", ascending=False)["PGS"].tolist()},
    template="plotly_white"
)
fig.show()

```


## table

```{python}

#make a pretty table with publications_meta_data

import plotly.graph_objects as go
fig = go.Figure(data=[go.Table(
    header=dict(values=list(publications_meta_data.columns),
                fill_color='paleturquoise',
                align='left'),
    cells=dict(values=[publications_meta_data[col] for col in publications_meta_data.columns],
               fill_color='lavender',
               align='left'))
])

fig.update_layout(title="Publications Metadata")
fig.show()
```
